We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts: 139.25, 134.60, 129.00 (x2), 128.30 (x2), 49.40, 26.10, 11.40.

We need number of CH3 groups in the compound. Methyl carbon typically appears around 10-15 ppm for aliphatic methyl attached to carbon (sp3). Here we have a signal at 11.40 ppm, likely a CH3. Also 26.10 could be CH2 or CH3 attached to something else (like isopropyl). 49.40 could be a carbon attached to heteroatom (like O-CH). The aromatic carbons are 128-139 region.

Thus likely only one methyl group (the 11.40 ppm). Could there be another methyl at 26.10? 26 ppm is typical for CH3 attached to carbonyl (acetyl) or to aromatic? But typical methyl attached to aromatic (toluene) appears ~21 ppm. 26 could be a CH2. But we need to determine number of CH3 groups. Use proton NMR maybe to confirm.

Let's get proton NMR.
